title: Schneider PowerLogic PM5560 Power Meter
description: Baseline model for the Schneider PowerLogic PM5560 power meter (METSEPM5560), read over Modbus RTU (RS-485) and Modbus TCP (Ethernet); it applies to meters that report the text PM5560 in the meter model registers 50-69. Register map: PM556x public Modbus register list of 10 August 2023 (sheet Register List, rows marked Y in the PM5560 column; its revision sheet gives firmware 4.1.8 for the PM5560), with the 4Q FP PF and data type definitions of its Data Types sheet. BLOCKING CONFLICT to settle on hardware: the register list and the user guide HRB1684301-18 give a 'Register' number and do not state whether the request carries that number or one less, and no example frame settles it. The model reads the number as a register number and subtracts 1 for the zero-based address (register 3000 is address 2999), because the same manufacturer's iEM3100/iEM3200/iEM3300 user guide DOCA0005EN-16 (PDF page 56) lists the same register numbers for the same quantities (3000 current, 3204 total active energy import, 4196 rate A energy) and states 'register = address + 1', and because Schneider's FAQ FA332210 says that some meters publish lists that need a shift of one. A read of the meter model text at address 49 (register 50) against address 50 settles it. Registers are read with function code 03 (holding registers; the manual's examples and FAQ FA241856 use holding registers). 32-bit and 64-bit values take consecutive registers with the high-order register first: Schneider's FAQ FA275749 states that PM5000 series meters store data most significant register first (big endian). Values the meter cannot supply read as the N/A value of their type (a float NaN 0xFFC00000). Left out: configuration and setup, the command interface, alarms and alarm logs, minimum and maximum values, per-harmonic magnitudes and angles, K-factor, crest factor, the second set of THD values (rows named 'thd'), data logs, timekeeping, serial number, manufacturer, meter name and hardware revision strings, the float copies of the energy values, the per-rate energy of the input metering channels, and the IEC 61000-4-30 data.
